slides.texte_overlay:
Unsexy money habits that
make your 30s easier
Track every expense for one month. Write down every coffee and every subscription. You'll be shocked at where your money really goes.
Have separate accounts. One for bills, one for spending, one for savings. Splitting your money makes overspending much harder.
Set savings goals with names. "Trip to Japan," "New car," "Emergency fund." Named goals are easier to stick to than vague savings.
Buy used when it makes sense. Furniture, books, tools, a first car. Quality second-hand items save a fortune and last just as long.
Before: I spent money to feel better. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I feel better without spending anything.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I spent money to feel better. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I feel better without spending anything.

slides.texte_overlay: Review your contracts every year. Phone, internet, insurance. A quick call to ask for a better deal often saves a lot. Ask once a year.
Give yourself a small fun budget. Saving everything leads to burnout. A little guilt-free spending keeps you on track long term.
